text:
elaine: seeing a p95/p99 spike on hosted API in eu-west-1 starting ~10:10 UTC, p95 jumped from ~420ms -> 1.9s, p99 up to 2.6s. noticed queue_depth climbs to ~120 on inference-worker-42. :eyes:

mike: who owns that worker pool? any deploys around then?

elaine: routing shows traffic still on model:redwood-v2-ctl, no deploys. scheduler metrics show coalescing window shrinking and average_batch_size dropped from 18->6 around the same time.

sre-oncall: logs from the task supervisor show several kernel fallbacks around 10:09: ``KernelSelector: fallback_to_generic=true reason="incompatible_batch_shapes"``

perf-bot: perf regression detector flagged kernel_switch_rate spike (x12) and kvcache_eviction_rate increase (x8). attaching recent profiler snapshot id=pf-2055006.

carmen: hmm incompatible_batch_shapes -> likely mixed short/long seqs causing batch sampler to emit small, heterogeneous batches. small batches -> more kernel fallbacks. Any change in request length distribution?

elaine: yes — request_len distribution shifted: 60% short (<64) and 40% long (>1024) during the window. Before it was 85% short. Also one tenant (tenant-id: t-311) went from 50 rps -> ~900 rps in that timeframe.

mike: noisy tenant. Did throttles fire? rate limiter shows that tenant was under soft-rate-cap but not hard-capped. our batcher doesn't isolate by tenant so mixes them. That can create a lot of stray KV cache misses for long sequences.

infra-bot: metric snapshot: inference_queue_depth{pool="eu-west-1-standard"}=118; avg_batch_size=6.2; kernel_generic_pct=67%; kvcache_hit=0.72 -> 0.44 during spike.

elaine: profiling heap on the worker shows KV cache churn: eviction_count increased sharply and prefetch_queue length oscillating. eviction traces show evicting prefixes for popular short sequences when long sequences come through, causing re-warm.

sarah: suggestion: short-term mitigation options: 1) apply per-tenant rate throttle to t-311, 2) pin kernel selection policy to prefer native kernels for known long sequences (disable fallback for a canary), 3) increase kvcache quota for the pool to reduce eviction churn. Which is least risky for prod?

mike: 1) quick and low risk — soft-throttle t-311 to bring them back to baseline. 2) pinning kernels is riskier since fallback protects from OOMs; need to test. 3) increasing kvcache memory affects host footprint and could cause pressure on other pools.

elaine: I'm leaning to throttling tenant + temporary sampler tweak: raise coalescing window to 25ms for eu-west pool to let more batching happen. That should raise avg_batch_size > 12.

perf-bot: estimated impact if avg_batch_size -> 12: per-token CPU drops ~1.9x, p95 expected to return to ~450-500ms in 30-60s after change (model-dependent).

carmen: can we apply both: ramp throttle 50% on t-311 + increase coalescing window to 25ms, monitor p95/p99 and queue_depth for 10m, then iterate?

sre-oncall: I can apply the throttle now. will also add a temporary alert for kernel_generic_pct>50% for 5m.

elaine: thanks. executing sampler update in 30s to 25ms on eu-west-1-standard pool. command I used: ``rctl update-sampler --pool eu-west-1-standard --coalesce-ms 25``

infra-bot: sampler update accepted by scheduler; rollout to workers in pool in progress (workers reporting commit=sha:ab12cf).

(1m later)

infra-bot: metrics: avg_batch_size=11.8; inference_queue_depth=26; kernel_generic_pct=22%; kvcache_hit=0.71.

elaine: p95 back to ~480ms, p99 trending down, queue depth stable. looks good so far.

sre-oncall: throttle applied to t-311 (soft 50% ramp). monitoring.

mike: we should follow up with a longer-term fix: 1) tenant-aware batching or tenant-scoped KV cache to prevent cross-tenant eviction, 2) smarter sampler that signals kernel selector about sequence-length heterogeneity to prefer homogeneous batches, 3) enforce per-tenant burst caps so a single tenant can't cause global batch shape variance.

carmen: agree. file a short RFC to product+infra proposing tenant-aware batching + per-tenant cache quotas. I'll draft and post to eng-runtime.

elaine: created quick postmortem doc (link: https://redwood.internal/ops/postmortems/2055006789) with timeline and mitigation steps.

sarah: note for next time: add a synthetic test that injects mixed-length traffic into a single pool to validate sampler and kernel selection under realistic burst patterns.

mike: +1. also add an alert on sudden shift in request_len histogram (e.g., median delta > 2x in 2m) so we catch noisy-tenant incidents earlier.

elaine: thanks all. I'll keep monitoring for 30m then revert the sampler back if stable. :thumbsup:
